USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

An antiemetic interaction in Parkinson disease

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A man with Parkinson disease uses intermittent apomorphine for disabling off episodes. He requests treatment for nausea associated with these injections. A prescription for ondansetron is stopped during medication reconciliation. Which adverse interaction is the strongest reason?

  1. Accelerated apomorphine elimination
  2. Pulmonary fibrosis
  3. Vitamin B12 malabsorption
  4. Profound hypotension and loss of consciousness
  5. Irreversible inhibition of monoamine oxidase
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Profound hypotension and loss of consciousness

Ondansetron and apomorphine are contraindicated together because severe hypotension and unconsciousness have been reported.

Understanding the options

Profound hypotension and loss of consciousness
Ondansetron and apomorphine are contraindicated together because severe hypotension and unconsciousness have been reported.
Irreversible inhibition of monoamine oxidase
Neither drug combination irreversibly inhibits MAO.
Accelerated apomorphine elimination
Loss of therapeutic effect from accelerated elimination is not the labeled concern.
Pulmonary fibrosis
Fibrosis is not the defining interaction.
Vitamin B12 malabsorption
B12 deficiency relates to prolonged acid suppression, not this combination.
